root_cause: The 22:12 cycle's hypothesis was that pool size and slot ownership decide flow, and it shipped one cold listing into the zero-row 'market research' pool (correctly, in 96 minutes - the fleet can ship). But the movement series of our three existing listings shows the real gate is one level up: per-listing weekly installs on skills.sh is a step function of the host repo's listing count - n=1 gives 0.0 installs/listing/week, n=2-3 gives 1.0 (exactly what our three cold listings earn), n=4-8 gives 6.6, and n=9-20 gives ~85. The competitor that owns our target pools runs a 40+ listing bundle where every skill earns thousands of installs, and its clones earn 1-12. So one listing in the right pool cannot cross the activation gate no matter how good the copy is, because the pool is not what carries the traffic - the bundle is. Our npm channel (ENEEDAUTH), our upstream catalog PR (#551, 0 reviews) and our social rail (mock adapter, 0 posts) are all human-gated, so bundle scale in a repo we own is the only lever that can move this week. The binding constraint is therefore listing count, not listing quality or pool choice.

experiment.hypothesis: Moving hypetopher/aicompany from 3 listings to 10 (n>=9) in one push moves per-listing weekly installs from our observed 1-2/wk to the 84.9/wk median of the n=9-20 band, because skills.sh flow attaches to the host repo's bundle rather than to the keyword pool a single listing sits in.
experiment.action: One push adding 7 new skills/*/SKILL.md listings to hypetopher/aicompany (plus the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json entries and README install lines that the 01:54 ship showed are required for indexing). Candidate family: the research / competitive-intelligence trigger words where our rows are 0 - market research, competitive analysis, competitor analysis, seo strategy, research report, market intelligence. Name rule: for every candidate, skills.sh search must show no listing with that exact name (or <=2 installs across all clones) - the 57 same-name families prove clones take scraps.
experiment.scope: 7 SKILL.md files + 7 manifest entries + README lines, one push, no code, no auth, no npm, no PR dependency, no listing published in our own 'growth intel' lane (we hold #1-#3 there with 0 flow)
experiment.metric: primary: weekly installs per bundle listing at day 7 (baseline: our cold listings 1-2/wk; band prediction at n=10 is ~85/wk/listing); secondary: count of bundle listings crossing the sum8>=7 activation gate; tertiary: repo total weekly installs (baseline 3/wk across 2 indexed listings)
experiment.baseline: our per-listing weekly installs = 1-2; repo indexed listing count = 2 (market-research-playbook pending index)
experiment.kill_criterion: if at day 7 every one of the 7 bundle listings shows <=5 weekly installs, repo bundle scale is NOT the driver - stop shipping listings, and escalate to the human-gated levers instead (npm login, PR #551 review, repair the social publish adapter)
